page: Microsoft Azure NC144lds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 144 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs paired with 264.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory configuration of 1.83 GB per vCPU. Computational acceleration is delivered by a single NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU equipped with 96 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Storage capability is anchored by 7972 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside support for Premium Storage. This provides rapid data staging and local read/write execution directly on the host, avoiding remote block storage bottlenecks for working data. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given the high vCPU count, dedicated core allocation, and 96 GB GPU memory capacity relative to the 264.0 GB host memory pool, the instance represents a specialized hardware density tradeoff. It is structured for GPU rendering, machine learning inference, and parallel simulation tasks that require substantial GPU memory and compute parallelism while remaining within moderate host RAM envelopes.
description: Microsoft Azure NC144lds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a specialized GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute-heavy visual and AI workloads. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supplies 144 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs alongside 264.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 1.83 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU featuring 96 GB of video memory. In addition to compute resources, the configuration integrates 7972 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial local scratch space for high-throughput input and output operations. The instance carries zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and supports Premium Storage. The architectural balance of massive core density, large accelerator memory, and modest system memory makes this server profile suited for GPU inference, parallel data processing, visual rendering pipelines, and simulation tasks where disk caching mitigates the restricted host-memory-per-core ratio.
